content.thinking:
I'm planning the golem's rig in a chunky toon style, around 2.6m tall, with a bone hierarchy starting at the hips and branching into spine, head, arms with fingers, and legs down to the feet.

I'm working through the exact joint and chain definitions carefully, placing hips, spine, neck, and head joints with specific coordinates and parent relationships, then adding a jaw joint for extra detail.

For the head itself, I'm sketching a boulder-like lump of basalt with a scaled sphere for the upper head, a lower box for the jaw, glowing eye parts, and a brow ridge. Then I'm defining the arm chains with shoulder, elbow, and wrist joints at mirrored x-coordinates, parented to the spine tip and tagged with an "arm" role.

For the hands, I'm adding fist boxes with chunky finger digits as small two-point chains, three fingers plus a thumb per hand, each contributing one joint, and working out how the wrist tip connects into the hand.

Now I'm laying out the leg skeleton with hip, knee, and ankle joints, attaching a foot box with toes at the ankle so the bottom sits flush at ground level, then starting the torso as a loft through the spine stations.

Writing crack and rock paint functions...

For the shoulder armor, I'm thinking hexagonal basalt columns made from six-sided cylinder geometry, stacked and clustered to look like natural basalt formations on the pauldrons.

For the chest, I want a glowing lava core sphere set into the torso, surrounded by a ring of small rock plates radiating outward using a line-frame arrangement to approximate a hexagonal housing around the glow.

Now I'm planning to add glowing molten seam details across the belly — thin glowing rods or plates tracing gaps between armor plates at the waist, giving the sense of cracked lava seams running through the body.

Extending this further, I'm reworking the limbs similarly: a glowing lava core running through the torso and limbs, surrounded by segmented rock plates with gaps so the molten color peeks through between them, using stacked cylindrical rock segments along the arm and leg chains.

Skinning with two-bone blending will work fine for the plate transitions. I'll keep plates rigid-ish along the lava sweep, sized by radius with uniform scale, and limit colors to stay under the flat-color cap. Now I'm starting to write the actual helper code, looping over each side with imports for the builder, frame, path, and paint utilities.

For the eyes, I'm thinking glowing slit shapes rendered as a texture decal on a plane placed on the face, giving an anime/Genshin-style glow without extra geometry complexity -- I need to be careful not to leave unused imports. I'm defining color constants for lava, gold, and obsidian basalt, then setting up mottled rock paint variations for the shoulder chips using the rng utility for scatter variety.

Now I'm refining the crack pattern logic so cracks only appear on certain cell regions based on noise thresholds, keeping the glowing lava veins subtle rather than overwhelming the surface, and adding darker rock tones plus gold filigree bands at the wrists and neck for that ancient golem aesthetic.

For the gold bands, I'm orienting torus rings around the limb axis correctly by aligning the tangent direction with the geometry's natural axis so they wrap cleanly around joints. Then I want to add a glowing rune texture for the chest and forehead glyphs.

For the belly rune, I'm working out the right placement against the hip octagon geometry so the glowing plane sits flush against the front surface without clipping, backed by a small plate for depth.

For the torso, I'm deciding to split the chest into left and right pec plates with a gap at center so the lava core sphere glows through, and I'm starting to define the loft stations for the core itself from hips up through the spine.

Now I'm adding the pelvis rock plating with hanging loincloth slabs, plus belly band plates along the spine joints, going for that gold-trimmed Genshin aesthetic.

Working out the chest piece next — pec boxes flanking a glowing core sphere with a gold torus ring around it, then starting on the back plating to match.

For the spine, I'm planning a row of five hex-shaped columns running down the back, tilted backward like basalt crystals with glowing cone tips, positioning them along the y-axis with a negative rotation to angle them away from the body.

For shoulders, I'm clustering five hex columns of varied heights as pauldrons, attaching them to the first joint of the arm chain so they move naturally with the limb.

Now I'm placing the head: a neck chain leading to the head joint, with the skull built as a faceted icosahedron boulder shape, and the jaw as a smaller wedge-like scaled icosahedron beneath it.

I'm adding jaw details—small cone teeth and tusks jutting upward, plus a glowing lava inset for the mouth—then positioning the glowing slit eyes on the front of the head using angled planes.

Positioning the sphere at z .49 with that depth so it stays visible across the surface. For the brows, I'm angling each rock slab with a sign-based rotation so the inner edges slope downward, giving that angry look, then moving on to planning hex-column crests for the head crown.

Adding glowing crest tips, gold earrings, and sketching out fist and finger geometry -- a fist box at the wrist, with each finger built as a short two-joint polyline swept into a tube shape and parented to the hand, plus a separate thumb chain.

Now I'm defining the arm chains from shoulder through elbow to wrist using catmull interpolation, with lava-core plates swept along at increasing radius toward the fists to give that heavy golem-arm look.

For the leg geometry, I'm applying the same along-chain plate technique across the hip, thigh, and shin points, using the frame orientation from the tangent to align each cylinder segment naturally.

The knees need a rock-textured hex cap with a gold ring accent, while feet get boxes plus three toe-box hexes with lava cracks and a heel. I'm deciding to skip floating ember particles since the "nothing hangs above the model" rule applies, but I'll keep a lava drip hanging from a limb for detail.

Adding small rock chip shards scattered over the torso surface using cone geometry, filtered so they don't cover the glowing core too heavily, capped around 30 instances. I'm settling on a dark flat color for jaw/rock areas and organizing the stick/ring helper signatures for placing these elements.

Now I'm working through glow wrapping for parts and sweeps, verifying mesh materials won't break the glow function. I'm checking floor contact heights for feet and toes, and totaling the golem's overall height to confirm realistic proportions around 2.8 meters.

Now I'm defining helper geometry for hexagonal cylinder shapes, then placing the pauldron columns around each shoulder with staggered offsets and outward tilts to avoid clipping into the head.

Chest comes from the spine tip, with spine1 as the first joint. I'll skip detailed eye geometry in favor of spheres, and place the rune texture on a pelvis front plate instead of the belly—using a glowing plane facing outward on the loincloth slab.

I'm sizing the pelvis box and loincloth hanging slabs to fit between the thighs, then drawing the rune as an SVG with a diamond cross pattern and glowing circle accent.

Now I'm adding a lava-rock hex collar piece on the chest and figuring out how to sweep glowing lava around the neck chain. I'm defining a reusable column helper function for the back support beams, using flat geometry shading, then positioning a glowing cone tip along a direction vector for the crown.

Still working through rotation math...

I'm adding a couple fist drips, then assembling the full file, double-checking the typing for chain/path callbacks and setting up a surface scatter for hit decals.

I need to trim unused imports carefully, keeping only what's used, and define the gold trim color for the paint call before writing everything out.
